observer: Claude (Opus 5.5), 9 Nov 2026: the raw scan (2926 x 2083) blurred 3x3, in overview and six tiles with a 0.02 grid; the casting's rim read by eye at 31 points from the tiles and an ellipse fitted to them with OpenCV
covers: the turret's underside seen from below, the camera low and looking up and aft through the roof's opening over the top of the 0096-9M2: the whole opening's outline except where the cabinet and the grey casing hide its aft end, the roof lining round it with its ragged edge, the white collar and black layer where the cloth is gone, the olive casting with its ribs, gearbox arm, covers and switchbox, the boot's top, the grey casing behind the cabinet
notes: VEHICLE: interior session A (g097-g100, a 9A33BM2/BM3, not identified further: the catalogue's 'session A'), NOT the ex-NVA 9A33BM3-1 of the hangar session (g082-g096). Everything matched to g096-a below is a cross-session match: same type, may differ on the individual vehicle. Orientation: image bottom is aft (the cabinet), image top is forward and overhead, image left is the vehicle's right (the same as g096-a, which looks aft). THE OPENING'S OUTLINE: a smooth closed curve with no straight run and no corner; 31 rim points read by eye fit a single ellipse to 8.6 px rms (largest 24 px) on a major axis of 2696 px, residuals with no pattern. Centre (0.527, 0.581), major axis within about 2 degrees of image-horizontal, so across the vehicle. Minor/major 0.63 in the image; if the rim is a circle the camera looks about 51 degrees off its axis, which is plausible for a camera low in the aisle looking up and aft. The photo alone cannot tell a circle from a plan ellipse: any ellipse is a view of a circle. Two things argue for a circle: the casting is the rotating part and turns inside a fixed lining with a thin even gap, and the boot's top sits at the fit's centre. The aft end of the rim (y over 0.88) is behind the cabinet and casing and was not seen. g096-a's 'wide ellipse' is this rim seen much flatter. Against g096-a: the switchbox, its chain, the tan cylinder, the grey plate and the casing are all at the same side of the boot in both sessions; the white cord differs (here on the boot's right-hand edge in the image, tied to the hem; in g096-a a loose loop hangs left of the boot beside a cable), and the lining here is pale where g096-a's is dark grey-green (flash and grime may explain that). The catalogue's 'quilted rim' is not stitched quilting: no stitch line or regular grid is visible anywhere, only puckers and folds in a padded cloth.

details.what: the true outline of the roof's opening as seen here, the casting's outer rim where it meets the lining's edge across a thin dark gap: a smooth closed curve, no straight run, no corner (ellipse fit in notes); lower-left arc, then up the image-left side, over the top, down the image-right side; the aft arc between the two ends is hidden by the cabinet and casing
details.size_cue: across the image about three times the boot's top width
details.note: same physical thing as g096-a d06-d08 (cross-session match); the model's stand-in is a dark ellipse

details.what: the lining's inner edge along the top of the opening: the cloth comes down in a soft thick roll and ends in a ragged, slightly curling edge a hand's width from the first fold, a thin black gap between it and the casting
details.size_cue: the gap about as wide as the blue cable

details.what: the lining's inner edge down the image-right side below the torn part: thick, soft, brown-stained where it meets the rim, a gap showing a dull brown edge
the lining's inner edge down the image-left side and under the flange, a soft dark band of grime against the rim

where the cloth is torn away at the top right, a white-painted metal collar round the opening is bare: a smooth band following the rim, between the casting's gap and the black layer, ending in a pointed corner at its right end
details.size_cue: about as wide as the blue-grey switchbox's end
details.note: the collar is what the lining's edge is fixed round; it would be under the cloth elsewhere

details.what: two rust-haloed round screw heads in the bare collar

pattern.note: spacing about a tenth of the rim's visible top arc; more are likely under the cloth

details.size_cue: each about the size of the switchbox's knob

details.what: a black band of woven or felt layer exposed where the cloth has gone, running with the collar above it: under-layer of the lining (register calls it a rubber strip along the rim; the weave and the way the cloth has pulled off it read more as felt than rubber)
details.size_cue: about as wide as the collar
details.note: the register's lining.turret_ring_seal_strip; black layer visible only where the cloth is missing. Rubber or felt not resolved

details.what: the torn left end of the bare stretch: the cloth's cut edge drawn back in a raised lip, with a small tear and a lifted flap at about the middle of the top rim
the roof's lining round the opening: a pale, matt, soft cloth, off-white to pale grey-green, a thick soft body to it
details.note: g096-a d09's lining is the same thing (cross-session match) though much darker there; the model's roof is a flat colour

details.what: the padding's relief: soft puckers and small rounded dimples in a broken row drawn in towards the rim, and long soft folds; no stitch lines, no regular quilting grid

pattern.note: about eight dimples visible along this arc

details.size_cue: a dimple about as wide as the switchbox's knob

details.what: longer soft diagonal folds in the lining at the image-left side, running out from the rim towards the wall
the grime band round the rim: the lining darkens to a sooty grey for about the last hand's width to its edge, all round the visible rim
a welted seam in the lining at the upper left, a raised pale strip curving from the top edge inward

a dark straight crease with a light strip beside it across the top-left corner of the frame: a seam or the lining's join to the upper side wall, not a transverse beam (the beam in g096-a d01 is out of frame here)
a small bright tie or tag standing out of the lining's edge at the rim
details.size_cue: about twice as long as a collar screw's head is wide

details.what: the casting's paint: bright yellow-olive, glossy, pale chalk lines on the raised edges and the ribs
details.note: much greener and brighter than g096-a's dark ring; flash and session both differ

details.what: the casting's outer rim: a raised rounded band following the opening's edge, an inner dark arc of shadow on the far side of it round the image-left
details.size_cue: the band about as wide as the flange's cap

details.what: a main rib of the casting running from the flange across to the boot, a raised bar with a chalked edge and a deep shadow on its far side
a transverse rib from the casting's top edge toward the boot, two close parallel ridges forming a shallow groove down the middle of the casting
a long diagonal rib or web edge below the rod, running down and right towards the switchbox, its shadow a thin black line
a green round cap on a heavy bolted flange at the casting's rim at the image-left, standing proud down into the compartment, about six hex bolts round it
details.size_cue: the flange's diameter about the width of the switchbox
details.note: probably g096-a d18, its olive drum with three studs (cross-session match; g096-a sees it from the side)

details.what: a long plain pale rod from a socket in the casting beside the flange up to the handle block, straight, about a third of the opening's width
details.size_cue: about three times as thick as the blue cable, and about a quarter of the opening's width long

details.what: the lever's head: an olive arm from a chrome-capped end at the rim down to a small cast block with three pale buttons and a slot, on a chalk-outlined plate

details.what: the small blue-grey switchbox on the casting left of the boot, sloped face, rounded plan, a plain lower side with white stencil; a chain hangs from a tab at its lower left

details.what: blue cable run with white ties across the casting: from the flange up to the lever head, and branching across to the switchbox and on over the boot to the arm

details.what: the same blue cable going on: from the switchbox's side round the corner by the boot to the arm's plate
the gearbox arm: a heavy olive casting from the brass port across to the disc housing, one long box-section lobe with chalked ribs, and an outer lobe wrapped round beside the opening's edge

details.what: the round brass port on the arm: a flange with screws and a recessed cupped centre

details.what: the tan cast unit: a large cylinder angled down out of the casting, ending in a brass head with an octagonal ring and a hinged loop, its domed glass or end cap dull
a second tan drum under the arm's root, stencilled in two lines, a grey plate on its side, standing proud over the boot

details.what: the round cover on the arm, six slotted screws round its edge, a bright chalked rim

details.what: a small rectangular plate on the arm beside the round cover, chalk outlined, with a short stencil
a shallow crescent-shaped recess of the casting beyond the arm's lobe, a dark curved slot with a loop of thin wire and a bolt in it
two black rubber blocks side by side on the casting's lower right, a stencilled number between them

details.what: the boot: grey rubberised fabric over the central column, seen from under its top, large soft folds, a darker grey-blue hem band round its top

details.what: a thin blue-grey cable along a bracket at the bottom left of the frame, clipped by stud heads, below the tan cable
